items.what: Merging now spends as few boxes as pay, the largest first. Among choices with the same box count, the one with a box a mix moved wins. A box of unknown making always goes after every other box. Round four's Fund and Pay ranks still pick the one box that pays alone (step 1); they no longer order merges. The rule lives in one place in seedelf-core/src/build.rs: `box_rank` (:2561, pub) gives 0 for mixed, 1 for boxes alone, 2 for unknown making. `boxes_largest_first` (:2574) is the static order: known boxes largest first, then unknown making. `more_mixed` (:2584) lists the same-count choices with more mixed boxes, most first. `boxes_to_merge` (:2609, pub) is the parts' order for a gap. In `apart`, orders a and b (by_history, by_tier) and c (fewest_boxes) all place boxes by that one order (`place`, :3045-3095). `grow` now reports where it built (`Grown::Built(T, usize)`, :2861). After any of a, b or c builds with j boxes, `more_mixed_built` (:2889, called at :3160) tries the same count with more mixed boxes first, regrowing c's other inputs; the first that builds wins, else the original build, so nothing new is refused. The CLI's blind order d is unchanged. With tokens sent, a box of the tokens' own class counts as mixed (it adds no history). Mint follows the same box order. In the WebAssembly (wasm/src/lib.rs:4135-4176), Worth::apart orders its tier-2, token-free classes by `build::boxes_to_merge`, with gap = owed minus what the non-box histories add; tier-2 classes holding tokens come after them. Docs updated: Origin::Lovejoin, Purpose::Pay and Fund, rank()'s comment, tier(), rank_of, select_script_inputs step 3, the orders comment, the stale 'a grew these already' line (:3120), and Worth::apart's doc.

strings.en: Paid from your private balance, one of its UTxOs of ADA alone goes into the box's own transaction, and its ADA comes back with the box, less the fee, so anyone can tie that UTxO, and where it came from, to the box. Where it can, the wallet takes one marked only Back from Lovejoin.
strings.es: Si pagas con tu saldo privado, uno de sus UTxO solo de ADA entra en la propia transacción de la caja, y su ADA vuelve con la caja, menos la comisión, así que cualquiera puede vincular ese UTxO, y de dónde vino, con la caja. Siempre que puede, la billetera usa uno marcado solo como “De vuelta de Lovejoin”.

policy_facts: Merging boxes (a funding, a top-up, a Send, a Make public, a stealth mint, a pool's start, and a payment's parts): the wallet spends as few boxes as pay, the largest first. Among choices of as many boxes, it takes the one with a box it knows a mix moved. A box it can't tell the making of (tagged Unknown too, a planted box's way back among them) goes after every other box, even where that merges more boxes. Choosing one box that pays alone is unchanged: for a funding and a private payment, a box it knows is mixed before any other. So the 18 November sentence ('takes a box it knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of') holds for one box; for merging it should say 'as few as pay, a mixed one first among as many, one it can't tell the making of after every other box'. Nothing new is sent or kept.

Escape hatch, paid from the private balance: the payer is a box a mix moved first, then another box whose making the wallet knows (a way back 1.9.1 kept with no record among them), then the rest. Of the rest, where the box is a public account's, one made private from no other public account comes first; then the smallest that pays. The note under the payer now says 'one marked only Back from Lovejoin'. Nothing new is sent or kept.

B7: a site whose page leaves its connect question, or its wait for the unlock, unanswered is now always kept with the sites declined (session storage) and waits out the back-off. The one exception: another of its pages has enable() running, waiting on that question, on the unlock before it, or still on its way to it. Another page waiting for the unlock to sign or send no longer spares it. The policy's 'unless another of its pages is asking to connect too' now holds as written. No new kind of data is kept: only the decline records the policy already describes, which these cases now also write.

Facts for R5-docs (their architecture.md:144, :565, privacy.md:173, :432 and flows.md:377, :526 already match the code):
- Final merge order. Orders a, b and c take boxes in one order for every purpose, Mint included. First come boxes whose making the wallet knows (origin mixed, or every id part `box:`), largest first, so as few as pay. Where an order builds with j of them, the choice of j with the most mixed boxes that also builds goes instead; c's other inputs are regrown for it. Then boxes of unknown making (any id part other than `box:`), largest first, after every other box. With tokens sent, a box of the tokens' own class counts as mixed. Step 1, one UTxO alone, is unchanged and is the purpose's rank. A payment's parts (Worth::apart) order the token-free tier-2 classes by boxes_to_merge(gap = owed minus what the non-box histories add): the fewest that cover the gap, of those the most mixed, then the other known boxes largest first, then those of unknown making; tier-2 classes holding tokens come after them.
- The hatch's order. A box a mix moved first. Then other boxes alone (knownBox, 1.9.1-era plain ways back among them). Then the rest, where the box is a public account's, one naming no other public account first. Then the smallest. The WebAssembly spends the first that pays.
- The spare rule. Only another live page with an enable() running spares the site (`enabling`: waiting on the question, on the unlock before it, or on its way to it). Any other unlock wait spares nothing. Leaving any unlock wait still counts as a decline. The unlock still clears a mark set by a page leaving its unlock wait, and keeps one set by a page leaving its connect question.

policy_facts: This round I own the policy and wrote it myself. Every change sits inside the unshipped 18 November 2026 entry and the two body passages it describes (the Lovejoin row :28 and the Koios bullet :44). The Effective line is unchanged and there is no new date.

Nothing new is sent or kept by these words. They say what the code at 1e1b0647 already does: each later pool read that counts your boxes (opening Lovejoin's page, any Bring one back press, the wallet's own runs at an unlock or a due time) asks again about a box the Cardano server hasn't answered for yet, until it answers. Koios gets the request; our server answers from its listing.

Bring one back anyway takes the box it's pressed for without that question, and so does a box coming back by itself from a retired pool. But the pool read before each asks again about any box not answered for yet, and that is the box Bring one back anyway takes first where there is one.
Bring every box back now in Settings, Bring every box in this pool back now on a pool's page, the retired pools' run and Pay from my private balance anyway take a box without that question.

For a 1.9.1 answer saying a deposit made a box still in a current pool, the once-more ask takes in, in the same request, that pool's other boxes of yours the wallet has no record or answer for. privacy.md also says the restore-case form: while a box is held for an answer, each such read asks about the pool's other unrecorded boxes too.

Bringing a box back paid from the private balance takes a box the wallet knows is mixed before one it can't tell the making of, as a session's funding and a private payment do (R5-code's l4code#2, now in the 18 November entry).
